transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-03-03
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 min
Attendees: Samir Gupta (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Mariner PL), Roberto Diaz (Mariner Eng), Nina Park (Mariner CTO), Luis Ortega (Mariner DevOps)

Summary: quick live run of Hosted API chat + console quick tour + Optimize suggestions. Lots of back and forth on latency vs cost and how to measure tail lat. Some transcription noise, names sometimes misattributed.

[00:00:08] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're gonna keep this tight, two parts — quick hosted api walk through, then a console/optimize piece. if any time please interrupt.
[00:00:26] Maya: thanks, yeah we only have 50 minutes so appreciate that. main thing for us is, we want a chat assistant inside our checkout flow but need <low latency> less than 250ms p50 ideally, and cost constraints.
[00:00:40] Samir: totally, that's exactly the tradeoffs we'll hit. quick question on current stack — are you calling any external llm infra today?
[00:00:48] Roberto: right now we have a small internal lambda hitting openai for prototyping. it's ok but spikes are expensive. we also care about data residency for EU users.
[00:01:02] Lena: okay good, that maps — hosted api can run in region, we also have dedicated/private if you need VPC or on-prem. today we'll focus on hosted flow.
[00:01:16] Priya: quick note on tokens — when you think cost, prompt length and caching matter a lot. prefix caching can save a bunch if you have repeated system prompts.
[00:01:29] Maya: can you show streaming? we rely on streaming to render partial replies in the UI.
[00:01:34] Samir: yep we'll demo streaming and how the SDK handles reconnects and retries.

[00:03:10] Samir: (shares screen) here's the sandbox quickstart — the chat endpoint supports streaming chunked events. when you start a stream you get deltas; the SDK has automatic retry logic with exponential backoff.
[00:03:30] Lena: important detail: default retry is 3 attempts with jitter, and we surface an idempotency key option if you want exactly-once semantics for non-streaming ops. for streaming you usually do client side merging on reconnect.
[00:03:48] Luis: so if there's a network blip will the response start over? how do we avoid duplicate tokens showing to users?
[00:03:55] Priya: good q — typical pattern is to use prefix cache + client merge. we keep the last known token index and resume from there. the SDK returns resume hints. it's not perfect — occasional duplication possible, but we give helpers.
[00:04:15] Maya: and how about parameters — temperature, top_p, max_tokens — what's the impact on latency?
[00:04:22] Lena: temperature/top_p mostly affect output diversity, not raw latency. max_tokens obviously impacts total tokens returned. latency is mostly model size, sequence length, and batch behavior on the server.
[00:04:36] Roberto: can we control batching? we need low latency for checkout, but maybe background tasks can use batching for cost savings.
[00:04:44] Priya: yes — Redwood Optimize can recommend batching windows per route. for low-latency routes we suggest immediate mode (no batching) and smaller model variants; for async we batch 50-150ms to get throughput gains.

[00:07:02] Samir: showing console now — model catalog, per-model perf metrics, token cost breakdown per request, and a latency distribution chart. you can pin model versions and set rollout percent for canary.
[00:07:20] Maya: that chart is helpful — can we see p50/p95/p99 per route?
[00:07:26] Lena: yes routes have their own view, and you can filter by seq length. that helps identify tail latency caused by long contexts.
[00:07:38] Nina: for compliance we need audit logs and KMS integration. where does that sit?
[00:07:44] Samir: audit logs are in the console — available for Private and Dedicated with extended retention; hosted has audit logs but with retention tiers. KMS/HSM is supported for Private; for hosted we integrate with managed customer KMS for enterprise customers via key wraps, but we can surface the details in the security pack.

[00:10:12] Roberto: what's the SLA for hosted?
[00:10:16] Rajiv: hosted has best-effort; dedicated has SLA with uptime and latency SLOs. most customers start hosted, run a pilot, then move to dedicated if they need strict SLOs.
[00:10:30] Maya: ok that might be our path. pilot first.

[00:12:00] Samir: quick live request demo — I'm going to call chat.create with streaming true, temp .2, top_p .9, max_tokens 160. watch the stream and the token cost in the console.
[00:12:15] (streaming playback)
[00:12:40] Priya: note the token cost meter updates in near-real time; we also show estimated cost per 1k requests at current model/parameters.
[00:13:05] Luis: do you recommend temperature near zero for checkout suggestions?
[00:13:10] Lena: yes, for deterministic UX keep temp 0-0.2, top_p 0.7-0.95 based on how conservative you want replies. tune with your eval prompts.

[00:15:50] Maya: what about retries — if the call times out should we retry from UI? risk of duplicate actions (charging user twice etc.)
[00:15:58] Priya: for idempotent operations you can retry safely using idempotency keys. for UI flows that can trigger side-effects, best to have backend own the call and use server-side idempotency. UI should show pending state and not retry blindly.
[00:16:18] Roberto: what's your recommended backoff policy?
[00:16:22] Lena: exponential backoff with jitter, start at 200ms, cap at 2s, 3 attempts; but we tune per route. Optimize will surface retry impact on cost/latency.

[00:20:10] Samir: switching to Optimize — this is the suggestions view based on workload. we'll run a quick example: for checkout we suggest a smaller LLM quantized profile, prefix caching for the system prompt, and a 50ms batching window for certain low-priority enrichment calls.
[00:20:34] Priya: also shows regressed quality alerts tied to eval prompt sets. if you deploy a model variant and it drops quality we flag it.

[00:23:45] Maya: is quantization supported for all models?
[00:23:49] Lena: not all models; we have recommended quant profiles by model family. Optimize proposes which quant to use given latency targets and reproducers.

[00:26:10] Roberto: can we run a perf benchmark? we want p50 < 250ms and p95 < 600ms for our 16 token prompts.
[00:26:20] Samir: yes we can run a hosted benchmark — we'll need your traffic sample and a few synthetic prompts. we usually run a 48-72 hour run to capture tail.
[00:26:33] Maya: could Dedicated be cheaper at scale?
[00:26:36] Priya: often yes — at sustained throughput Dedicated can lower cost per token and improve tail latency. Optimize will give an ROI estimate.

[00:30:05] Nina: security again — SOC2, ISO, SSO. we also need data residency in eu-west-1.
[00:30:12] Samir: we'll send the security pack — SOC2 report, ISO attestations, SAML/SSO integration guide, VPC options for Private. for EU residency we can deploy hosted endpoints in eu-west-1 and set routing policy.
[00:30:30] Luis: what's data retention defaults on hosted?
[00:30:34] Rajiv: default short-term retention for metrics; you can opt into no retention for prompts/outputs under enterprise contracts. we'll detail in docs.

[00:33:05] Samir: quick Q&A — Maya: how to instrument the SDK for token cost per user?
[00:33:12] Priya: insert the token header from the response; console also shows per-request breakdown and you can export. we recommend a per-route tagging scheme.

[00:36:40] Roberto: if we hit a weird 500 rate in peak will Redwood auto-fallback to a cheaper model or different region?
[00:36:47] Lena: yes Smart Routing can fallback to compatible model variants or region based on policy; you configure priorities and fallback actions in the console.
[00:37:05] Samir: also we have graceful degradation patterns: return a cached answer, show partial, or route to lower-cost model.

[00:40:22] Maya: would you be able to share a short checklist for pilot success criteria?
[00:40:28] Samir: yes — I'll send a pilot checklist (latency targets, sample prompts, success metrics).

[00:44:10] Priya: notes on implementation: backend should own calls, use idempotency keys for side-effecting workflows, use streaming for UI latency UX, and configure short batching windows for low-latency endpoints.

[00:47:55] Maya: sounds good. next steps?
[00:47:58] Samir: recap — Samir to share pilot pricing + quickstart, Lena to share security pack, Roberto to send traffic profile. we'll schedule a follow-up SE deep dive next week.
[00:48:10] Roberto: aiming to start pilot next Monday.
[00:48:18] Nina: if pilot hits regressions we'll plan a dedicated sizing session.

[00:50:00] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links in email.
[00:50:08] (call ends)

Action items inside call: Samir to send pricing and checklist; Lena to send security docs; Roberto to share traces.
notes: Customer prefers hosted pilot before committing to Dedicated. Emphasis on p50/p95 tail benchmarking and evaluation prompts. Mentioned EU residency and KMS. Agreed to 2-week latency pilot and follow-up SE deep dive.
questions_raised: Will hosted meet p95 latency for 16-token prompts?
What's default retention for user prompts on hosted?
How to avoid duplicate tokens on stream reconnects?
closing_recap: Samir: Send pilot pricing + quickstart repo; Lena: Security pack; Roberto: Traffic samples. Schedule SE deep dive once data shared.
